source.quote: Ask: “The labelled graph has the form $y=a\lvert x+b\rvert+c$. Determine $a$, $b$ and $c$.” Supply exact points in accessible text as well as the graph, without showing recovered coefficients. `given_representation: graph`; `response_format: numeric` (a complete correctly positioned formula is an accepted equivalent).

supplementary_sources.quote: Must read: vertex, both zeros, $y$-intercept, $x/y$ directions, V/inverted-V orientation and the fixed plus-sign convention inside the modulus. Fixed: Cartesian axes, one vertex, straight arms and explicit coordinate labels. Variable: all point values, window, slopes and label offsets. Relations: slopes $-a$ left/$a$ right; symmetry $x=-b$; every point satisfies the same expression. Generate question/solution/reference assets from one tuple. Equal labelled grid units are used in the paper illustrations; no screen measurement is asked. No fixed source crop accompanies incompatible new values.

supplementary_sources.quote: Flat-classification, D1 redesign: $f(x)=a(x-h)^n+c$, supplied **expanded**, $n\in\{3,4\}$, $a\in\{-2,-1,1,2\}$, $h\in\{-2,-1,1,2\}$, $c\in\{-4,-3,-2,-1,1,2,3,4\}$. Starting with n3/4 and D0 shift sets gives360 raw combinations; remove h=0 to leave288, then c=0 (32) to leave **256**. The retained two-extrema domain has a polynomial coinciding with YM Try26(a), but this is disclosed mathematical overlap, not permission to reproduce that textbook exercise or its sketch subpart.

The flat stem is uncued: 'Find the exact coordinates of every stationary point and classify it as a maximum, minimum or stationary point of inflexion. Give sufficient evidence to justify the type and rule out the other types.' [point3, classification3]. Quartic is an in-scope power, not an unannounced new recipe.

source.quote: R3-07 diagram must-read givens: horizontal $x$, vertical $\ln y$, both exact labelled coordinates and their common straight line. Fixed: Cartesian axes, explicit logarithm, exact coordinate labels, schematic/no measurement. Variable: the exact model/point data, line direction and viewport. Relations: both points lie on $u=px+p+L$, $x_2>x_1$, negative/zero ordinates remain visible, and no hidden $A,p$ appear in labels or accessibility text. Zero-ordinate points need labels placed away from both line and axis. Labels must be offset to the side away from the line; **no opaque label box may cover the line**. Stage E/F must test bounding-box/line/axis intersection on every admitted presentation. The three current paper SVGs use offset transparent labels; they are static examples, not a runtime renderer.

Exact graph labels are $(x_i,u_i)$ on axes $x$ and $\ln y$, where $x_1\in\{1,2,3\}$, $x_2=x_1+d$ and $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $u_i=px_i+p+L$.
